title: Email & calendar
blurb: Outlook, Apple Mail and webmail: not sending, not syncing, password prompts, calendar trouble.

remedies.title: Attachments won't open from Outlook
remedies.why: The file type is blocked for safety, no app opens it, or the sender's mail turned it into winmail.dat.

steps.text: Save the attachment to a folder first, then open it from there.
Blocked types (.exe, .js) are blocked on purpose; ask the sender to share via a link.
winmail.dat: ask the sender to send in HTML or plain text, not Rich Text.

remedies.title: Outlook folders or messages disappeared
remedies.why: A folder got dragged into another, a view filter hides mail, or a rule moved it.

steps.text: Search all mailboxes for a known message and check which folder it's in.
View › Reset View (classic) removes filters hiding mail.
Check Deleted Items › Recover items deleted from this folder.
Look for a misplaced folder inside other folders.

remedies.title: Some emails go to "Other" instead of my Inbox
remedies.why: Focused Inbox sorts mail it thinks is less important into Other.

steps.text: View › Show Focused Inbox to turn it off, or move a message to Focused › Always move to Focused.

remedies.title: Meetings show twice or keep reappearing after deleting
remedies.why: The calendar is synced twice (two accounts or apps), or a delegate keeps the old copy.

steps.text: Check whether the same calendar is added twice (e.g. via iCloud and Exchange).
Delete or decline from Outlook on the web, then let devices sync.
Remove calendar sync from apps you no longer use on the phone.

remedies.title: Too much spam or newsletters
remedies.why: Genuine newsletters unsubscribe cleanly; real spam should be blocked, not answered.

steps.text: For newsletters you signed up for, use Unsubscribe at the top of the message.
For spam, use Report/Block sender; don't click unsubscribe links in obvious spam.
Report phishing with the Report button.

remedies.title: Send an email securely (encrypted)
remedies.why: Microsoft 365 can encrypt mail so only the recipients can read it.

steps.text: Outlook: Options › Encrypt (or Encrypt-Only / Do Not Forward) before sending.
For files, a password-protected PDF or a share link limited to named people is often simpler.

remedies.escalate: Your organisation may have rules for sensitive data; ask IT which option to use.

remedies.title: Let someone manage my email or calendar (delegate)
remedies.why: Delegates can read, send on behalf of, or manage your calendar.

steps.text: Outlook: File › Account Settings › Delegate Access (classic), or share the calendar with "Can edit" / "Delegate".
Send-on-behalf for the whole mailbox is set by IT.

remedies.title: The old Windows Mail app changed to Outlook
remedies.why: Microsoft replaced Mail and Calendar with the new Outlook for Windows.

steps.text: Open Outlook (new) from Start; it imports your accounts when you sign in.
Or use webmail, or another mail app.
